problemText: Which number-line graph shows the solution set of 5x - 3 >= 12?
hints: Solve it first: add 3 to both sides, then divide by 5 (positive, so no flip).
The symbol >= is inclusive, so the boundary value itself is a solution; shade the direction the final symbol points.
Collect the x terms on one side and the plain numbers on the other — adding or subtracting never flips the symbol.
One clean route: add 2x and add 13 to both sides to reach 21 > 7x, then divide by 7 and rewrite with x on the left.

problemText: A club has 240 dollars to spend on trophies. Each trophy costs 18 dollars, and the order also carries a one-time engraving fee of 30 dollars. What is the greatest number of trophies the club can order without spending more than 240 dollars?
hints: Let t be the number of trophies and write the total cost as an inequality: 18t + 30 is at most 240.
Subtract the 30-dollar fee first, then divide by 18 — and remember the club can only buy a whole number of trophies.

hints: Subtract 5 from all three parts, then divide all three parts by 4.

problemText: Which of the following describes the solution set of |4x + 3| >= -2?
hints: Before splitting into cases, ask what the smallest value the left side could ever take is.
An absolute value is a distance, so it is never negative — compare that fact to the -2 on the right.

problemText: Solve 3|x - 5| - 4 <= 14, then type as a number how many INTEGER values of x satisfy it.
hints: Isolate the absolute value first: add 4 to both sides, then divide by 3.
|x - 5| <= 6 becomes the band -6 <= x - 5 <= 6; add 5 to all three parts, then count the integers, including both endpoints.
